finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: If 'n' is very large, it could lead to an overflow when calculating the size of the vector.
finding.assumptions: The value of 'n' is controlled by the user or is derived from an untrusted source. The code does not check if 'n' exceeds the maximum size of the vector.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
Checked whether the variable 'n' could be an untrusted source. It is defined as a hard‑coded constant at line 55 (int n = 10;). Since it is not derived from stdin, argv, a file, network input, environment variables, or any public API parameter, it does not satisfy the first condition for a vulnerability. No other path can modify 'n' before it is used in the loop, and the loop bounds are therefore bounded by a compile‑time constant. Consequently, no integer overflow or wraparound can occur in the vector push_back operation.
No other checks or constant arguments influence the loop.
No reachable path leads to an overflow.
Thus the finding is refuted.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If 'n' is controlled by an attacker and used in a command execution context, it could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The value of 'n' is derived from an untrusted source and used in a command execution context.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the variable "n" is initialized to a compile‑time constant (line 55) and is never overwritten. No external input source is used to set its value. The code performs only integer arithmetic (rand() % 100) and does not invoke any OS command execution primitives such as system(), exec(), or popen(). Therefore there is no sink that could lead to OS command injection.

finding.title: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If 'n' is very large, it could lead to a heap-based buffer overflow when allocating memory for the vector.
finding.assumptions: The value of 'n' is controlled by the user or is derived from an untrusted source. The code does not check if 'n' exceeds the maximum size of the vector.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked source of 'n' – it is hard‑coded on line 55, not an untrusted input. No bounds check is required because vector push_back dynamically resizes, and no overflow can occur from a small constant value. No path from an external source to the sink exists.

finding.title: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
finding.trigger: If the pivot value is used in a cryptographic operation without proper handling, it could lead to weak cryptography.
finding.assumptions: The pivot value is used in a cryptographic operation.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code implements a standard quicksort algorithm.  The variable "pivot" is simply an element of the vector and is never passed to any cryptographic API.  The sink operation "swap(arr[i + 1], arr[high])" is a simple element exchange, not a cryptographic primitive.  No cryptographic function calls or key handling are present in the provided fragment, so there is no path from the pivot value to a cryptographic operation.  Therefore the reported CWE-398 claim is unfounded.
